title: WPMS/450/2002 of K.C. TIWARI Vs STATE and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 Writ Petition No. 450 (M/S) of 2002
 K.C. Tewari S/o Sri Kali Charan Tewari - Petitioner
 Vs.
 State of Uttaranchal through Secretary Ministry
 of Labour, Dehradun and others - Respondents
 Sri J.C. Pandey, Advocate for the petitioner
 Sri H.M. Bhatia, Brief Holder on behalf of State.
 Sri R.K. Raizada, Advocate for respondent No.4.
Hon'ble B.S. Verma, J. (Oral)
By means of this petition the petitioner has sought a writ in the
nature of certiorari for quashing the order dated 25.5.2001 passed by
respondent No.3- Deputy Labour Commissioner Kumaun Range,
Haldwani, Nainital. Further prayer has been made to issue direction to
State Government to exercise its power under Section 4-K of U.P.
Industrial Act and to refer the matter in dispute arising out of
termination of service of the petitioner for adjudication to an
appropriate court under the U.P. Industrial Disputes Act.
 Briefly stated the facts giving rise to this writ petition,
according to the petitioner, are that the petitioner was appointed by
the respondent employer in the post of packing Assistant on
22.4.1988 and since then he continuously worked upto the date of
termination i.e. 1.4.1998. According to the petitioner the termination
was totally illegal. The employer without complying the provisions of
Industrial Dispute Act, terminated the service of the petitioner. The
petitioner approached the Conciliation Authority and moved an
application U/S 2-A of U.P. I.D. Act before the Deputy Labour
Commissioner/Conciliation Officer on 4.8.1998. The case was
registered as C.P. Case No. 117 of 1998. The respondent employer
appeared before the court and filed W.S. The respondent employer
pleaded that the post of Junior Officer falls under the category of
Supervisor and hence the petitioner is not covered under the definition
of 'workman' as defined in U.P. I.D. Act. The petitioner also filed
rejoinder affidavit before the Deputy Labour Commissioner. The

2
Deputy Labour Commissioner after hearing the parties rejected the
reference on 25.5.2001.
 Aggrieved by the impugned order the petitioner has preferred
this writ petition.
 Counter affidavit has been filed by the respondent/employer. It
is specifically pleaded in the counter affidavit in para-15 that the
petitioner had knowledge of the decision of Deputy Labour
Commissioner holding that making of reference as in-expedient and
knowing and accepting the order dated 25.5.2001, the petitioner
approached the management of respondent No.4 for settling his all
claims relating to termination of service. In para-16 of the counter
affidavit it is mentioned that petitioner relinquished his claim of
employment in the company by filing an application dated 21.8.2001
resigning from service of company/ seeking voluntary retirement and
the management of company with a view to settle the subject-matter
of termination of services of the petitioner also agreed to release the
additional ex-gratia benefits of six months salary to the petitioner. In
para-17 of the counter affidavit it is pleaded that there exists no
industrial dispute between the petitioner and the respondent No.4,
even if any dispute ever existed at any time, the same also ceased to
exists when the petitioner relinquished his claim of employment and
the petitioner is guilty of suppressing material facts in the writ
petition.
 The petitioner also filed rejoinder affidavit and gave evasive
reply against the counter affidavit.
 I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the
record.
 By a perusal of Annexure No.7 filed with the writ petition it is
quite clear that the petitioner had received a sum of Rs. 85,730/- by
way of demand draft dated 22.8.2001. It is pertinent to mention here
that the petitioner has not approached this court with clean hands. He
has only assailed the reference order dated 25.5.2001. The petitioner
has not disputed the settlement of his claim with the employer as well
as the voluntary retirement whereas it is specific assertion of the
respondent employer that the petitioner has settled his claim with the
employer and he had moved application dated 21.8.2001 seeking

3
voluntary retirement and with a view to settle the subject-matter of
termination of service the petitioner also agreed to release the
additional ex-gratia benefits of six months salary which he had
received and no industrial dispute exists between the petitioner and
the respondent/employer. The only subject-matter in the present writ
petition which existed was reference order which was rejected by the
State Government. When the petitioner had taken voluntary retirement
and settled his dispute and had received ex-gratia payment in lieu of
his termination from service, there exists no dispute as on today
regarding termination of service after voluntary retirement of the
petitioner as the termination order stands revoked, therefore, prayer
made by the petitioner for referring the dispute for adjudication U/S
4-K of U.P. I.D. Act is of no avail. The writ petition lacks merit and
is liable to be dismissed.
 The writ petition is dismissed.
ISB (B.S. Verma, J.)
 20-02-2013
